title: Buttons to robot states
summary: whileTrue vs onTrue, asking the robot for a state, then watching it change.

say.never: A **binding** connects a button to a command. There are two kinds. `whileTrue` runs the command *as long as you hold the button* and stops when you let go. `onTrue` runs it **once** each time you press the button.
say.bit: `whileTrue` runs a command while the button is held; `onTrue` runs it once per press.

board.code:
driver.x().whileTrue(spinFanCommand);   // runs while X is held
driver.y().onTrue(ringBellCommand);     // runs once each Y press

steps.title: In your lesson: Two kinds of button

say.never: Your buttons don't talk to the shooter. They ask the **robot** for a state. `whileTrue` with `Commands.startEnd` asks for `SHOOT` while the right bumper is held and `DRIVE` when you let go. `onTrue` with `Commands.runOnce` does one thing per press: here, a pretend launch for the simulator.
say.bit: The right bumper asks the robot for `SHOOT` while held and `DRIVE` on release. `onTrue` runs once per press.
